subject: Geopolitics
title: Alliance Fatigue
description: A short lesson to help you apply Alliance Fatigue.

hook.text: After 20 years in Afghanistan, American voters asked: why are we still defending others when we have problems at home?

buildup.text: Alliance fatigue occurs when publics tire of foreign commitments. The benefits feel distant; the costs feel real.

discovery.text: Populism feeds alliance skepticism. Politicians win votes by promising to put their own country first, not allies.

twist.text: But retreating from alliances creates power vacuums. When the US pulled back, China and Russia advanced.

climax.text: Alliance fatigue is cyclical. Engagement, exhaustion, retreat, crisis, then re-engagement. History loops.

punchline.text: Alliances cost money and sovereignty. Going alone costs more.

quiz.question: What causes alliance fatigue in democracies?
options: Rising defense budgets crowd out domestic spending
Publics tire of foreign commitments whose benefits feel distant
Allied nations refuse to cooperate on trade
